hints: Look closely at the dashed line for left ventricle pressure around 0.2 s and ask yourself what must have just finished happening before it shoots steeply upwards.
Remember blood only flows from higher to lower pressure, so the ventricle can only fill while left atrium pressure is above left ventricle pressure and the atrioventricular valve is open.
walkthrough:
**Spot the filling phase on the graph**

Think simply first. The ventricle becomes full of blood during diastole when blood flows in from the left atrium. On the left side of the graph, before 0.2 s, both atrial (dotted) and ventricular (dashed) pressures are very low and close together.

Rule to use: blood flows down a pressure gradient, from atrium to ventricle.

**Find when filling must stop**

Filling must stop when the ventricle starts to contract. You can see this as the moment the dashed left ventricle line shoots almost vertically upwards at about 0.2 s. At that moment ventricular pressure rises above atrial pressure, so the atrioventricular (bicuspid) valve shuts.

That sharp rise marks the start of ventricular systole.

**Match this moment to period A**

Period A ends exactly at that sharp rise in ventricular pressure. So at the end of A, passive filling plus the little atrial push (the small dotted bump) has just finished, and the ventricle is at its maximum volume, ready to eject.

Conclusion: the ventricle is full at the end of A.

options.A: Correct. The end of A is just before ventricular contraction begins, so atrial emptying into the ventricle is complete and ventricular volume is maximal.
options.B: False. Period B is during ventricular systole when ventricular and aortic pressures are very high, so blood is being ejected and the ventricle is emptying, not full.
options.C: False. The end of C is when ventricular pressure falls sharply below aortic pressure, so ejection has just finished and the ventricle is at its emptiest.
options.D: False. Period D is ventricular diastole with passive filling, but atrial systole has not yet topped up the ventricle, so it is not yet completely full at the end of D.
